hints: Notice the $30 \, \Omega$ resistor is in series with the combination of $60 \, \Omega$ and $R$, and the same $0.12 \, \text{A}$ flows through the battery and the $30 \, \Omega$ resistor.
Use $R_{total} = V/I$ with $6.0 \, \text{V}$ and $0.12 \, \text{A}$ to find the total resistance, then subtract $30 \, \Omega$ to get the resistance of the parallel part.
For the parallel part, use $1/R_p = 1/60 + 1/R$ with $R_p$ in $\Omega$ and solve for $R$.
walkthrough: Find the total resistance seen by the battery using $R_{total} = V/I$. Here $R_{total} = 6.0/0.12 = 50 \, \Omega$.
The circuit is $30 \, \Omega$ in series with the parallel pair. So $R_{total} = 30 + R_p$, where $R_p$ is the parallel resistance of $60 \, \Omega$ and $R$.
Hence $R_p = 50 - 30 = 20 \, \Omega$. The parallel value must be less than either branch, which fits $20 \, \Omega$.

options.A: Gives $12 \, \Omega$ by miscombining the parallel resistors, not by satisfying $R_{total}=50 \, \Omega$ with $R_p = 20 \, \Omega$.
options.B: Gives $R_p = 20 \, \Omega$ in parallel with $60 \, \Omega$, so $R = 30 \, \Omega$ and total is $50 \, \Omega$.
options.C: Gives total resistance $30 + $ parallel value greater than $20 \, \Omega$, so total exceeds $6.0/0.12 = 50 \, \Omega$.
options.D: Gives parallel resistance $30 \, \Omega$, making total $60 \, \Omega$ and current only $0.10 \, \text{A}$, not $0.12 \, \text{A}$.
